name: Kyo-yaki overglaze
summary: Fine pottery from Kyoto that Nonomura Ninsei made at the kiln of Omuro. A thin crackle glaze takes enamel colours and gold in painted designs of flowers, hills and seasons.

philosophy.core_thesis: A Kyoto potter can make tea ware as rich as a screen painting: a thin body, a pale crackle glaze, enamel and gold.
design_principles: Throw a thin, smooth form on the wheel, with a wall of 3 to 5 mm.
Cover the form with a pale crackle glaze that is fired first at about 1100 °C.
Paint the design in enamel colours and gold on the fired glaze, and fire again at 800 °C.
Place the design to fit the form: wisteria down a tall jar, peony round a water jar.
Keep part of the glaze plain, so that the painted area has room.
Use the Kyoto court palette: green, blue, red, purple, black and gold.
Sign the base with the maker's seal, as the Omuro kiln did.
Make each piece one of a small set, for a tea master or a temple.
anti_patterns: A thick rough glaze with fire marks and no overglaze
A single plain colour with no painted design
A print or a transfer pattern in place of the brush
A heavy wall with a bent, wild form

form.shape: Tall tea jars, water jars, incense burners and tea bowls with a smooth round body. Each form gives a large field for the painter.
form.profile: A tall jar rises in a smooth shoulder and a short neck; a water jar is a round drum with two lugs; a bowl has a soft curve and a thin rim.
form.foot_and_rim: A small, neat foot ring with the seal of the kiln; the rim is thin and round, and a lid in matching ware or in lacquer fits the mouth.
form.proportion: A tea jar is 15 to 20 cm high; the wall is 3 to 5 mm thick, so the form is light and the glaze is thin.
rules: Throw a thin, round, clean form.
Paint a flowing design that wraps round the form.
Leave one third of the glaze plain.
Add gold to flowers and leaf edges.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, pale Kyoto clay that fires hard and takes a thin glaze. Keep a coarse rough clay out: the thin glaze needs a smooth ground.

methods: turning the wall thin when leather-hard
fitting the lid on the wheel
painting the design with a fine brush on the fired glaze
applying gold leaf or gold paint on the enamel
forming.joins: Lugs and knobs are made separately and luted with slip; the lid is thrown with the jar and ground to fit.
forming.details: A fine crackle in the glaze, a painted seal on the base, and gold highlights on flowers and leaves.

glaze.pattern: Wisteria, peony, pine and plum, hills and seasons in enamel green, blue, red and purple with gold lines on a cream crackle glaze.
glaze.gloss: Satin to soft gloss, about 40 to 80 GU; the enamel stands a little above the glaze.
glaze.wear: The enamel and the gold wear first at the rim and at the high parts of the painted flowers; the crackle takes a stain from tea.

palette.strategy: Cream ground, a rich enamel palette of green, blue, red, purple and black, and gold lines. The painting uses 4 to 6 colours.

firing.kiln: A small climbing kiln at the Omuro kiln near Ninna-ji temple, and a small muffle kiln for the enamel firing.
processes: bisque firing of the thrown and turned form
dipping in a clear crackle glaze
firing.scale: A few master potters, with a small workshop, made each piece for tea masters, temples and the court of Kyoto.
firing.signs: A fine crackle, a raised line of enamel, a gold edge and a seal on the base.

pieces.form: Tall jar with wisteria in enamel falling over the shoulder
Round drum with two lugs and a painted peony with gold edges
Thin bowl with a free brown brush design of grass and pine
Small jar in lead glaze with plum blossom in gold

positive: cream crackle glaze with enamel colours
enamel green blue red and purple
decorative Japanese screen-painting style on a jar

canonical_works.work: Tea jar with a pine design
Water jar with a peony design

emotion.target_response: A refined delight. The viewer sees a pale jar with a flowing painted design and admires the court taste of Kyoto.

use_cases: a brief for an ornate Japanese tea jar
a decorative object with seasonal flower painting
a museum label for Kyoto pottery
avoid_when: the brief needs a plain, rough tea bowl
the brief needs an unpainted surface
the brief needs a dark single glaze

modifiers.request: plain and rough, with no painted design
modifiers.how: Hand-build the form in raku clay and cover it in one black glaze, with no painting.

modifiers.request: European tea service, same gold and colour
modifiers.how: Change to soft-paste porcelain, add a spout and handle, and paint flowers with gilt lines.

wall_thickness.note: Kyoto wares are thin; thicker walls break the line of the painted jar.
